subject: literature
passage: Every spring, Hamza spent his afternoons in his uncle's cramped workshop in Gujranwala, watching him build kites from tissue paper and thin strips of bamboo. Uncle Tariq, who had been making kites in the same small room for nearly thirty ______ never measured anything. He simply held a sheet of paper up to the light, bent a strip of bamboo between his fingers, and knew exactly where to cut.
stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

explanation.why: The clause "who had been making kites in the same small room for nearly thirty years" adds extra information about Uncle Tariq. It opens with a comma after "Uncle Tariq," so it must close with a comma before the verb "measured."
explanation.A: Incorrect. Extra information that opens with a comma must close with a comma; a dash doesn't match.
explanation.B: Incorrect. A semicolon can't separate the subject "Uncle Tariq" from its verb "never measured."
explanation.C: Incorrect. Without a closing comma, the "who" clause is never set off, and it seems to continue into "never measured anything."
explanation.D: Correct. The comma closes the nonessential "who" clause, so the subject "Uncle Tariq" connects to its verb "never measured."
